name: background
description: Foundations contract for the background-treatment system: the bg--{color}[--pattern--{type}] class grammar, its foreground-color cascade, border-color overrides under backgrounds, and the pattern-image layer. UIDS owns the grammar and the color/pattern tokens; uids_base (SiteNow) is the downstream consumer whose Layout Builder background options select these classes. Not a component — no Vue file. It DOES own one Figma component set as of 2026-08-24 (`Backgrounds`, 170:55): a documentation surface for the class grammar, not an instanceable component. See changes[2].

figma.note: The governed surface is the component set `Backgrounds` (170:55, 16 variants, 800×300). All 11 tokensUsed entries are bound on it — solid fill, text, link, border — verified live 2026-08-24. The 16 doc frames (163:5 … 163:61) are SUPERSEDED but still present, pending deletion by hand: see changes[2](f). The pattern layer is an IMAGE paint and a Figma variable is COLOR/FLOAT/STRING/BOOLEAN, so no pattern can ever be bound or verified by any checker — it is governed by instruction only, via the set description and rules.json's backgrounds-by-class.

options.name: color
options.description: Background color of the wrapping element. No default: the absence of any bg--{color} class IS the page-default background (semantic color/background), not a member of this enum. Combines with `pattern` into the single frozen class bg--{color}[--pattern--{type}] — see identity.description and knownIssues for why the grammar itself is the versioned shape.

code.notes: shared/background.ts exposes two prop shapes over this grammar: props.background (colors array ['', 'black', 'gold', 'gray', 'white'], addBackgroundClass prefixes 'bg--') for color-only consumers, and allBackgroundProps.background (allBackgroundOptions, 16 literal combo strings like 'gold--pattern--particle') for consumers that also expose pattern. Neither prop shape composes color+pattern independently at the JS layer — the combined string IS the value; there is no code path that ORs a separate color prop with a separate pattern prop.

options.name: pattern
options.description: Background image pattern layered over `color`. 'none' omits the --pattern--{type} suffix entirely (bg--{color} alone). 'community' and 'particle' are color-tinted PNG photographic textures; 'brain' is a solid-color SVG line pattern. See geometryNotTokenized for the fixed background-size per pattern and knownIssues for the full asset-per-combo map (some combos share an image file).

code.notes: Values above are the SUFFIX fragment appended to the color class (bg--{color}--pattern--{type}), not a standalone selector — 'none' adds no suffix. See the `color` option's code.notes for how shared/background.ts actually exposes the two axes as one combined prop string.

geometryNotTokenized.pattern-image-assets: 12 url() references (11 distinct files in use — community-pattern--gray.png is shared by gray and white, see knownIssues) in _background-mixins.scss's $backgrounds map ($imgpath = '../../assets/images', _variables.scss:26): bg--black--pattern--brain -> brain-pattern-black.svg (L10); bg--black--pattern--community -> community-pattern--black.png (L15); bg--black--pattern--particle -> particle-pattern--black.png (L20); bg--gold--pattern--brain -> brain-pattern-reversed.svg (L30); bg--gold--pattern--community -> community-pattern--white.png (L35); bg--gold--pattern--particle -> particle-pattern.png (L40); bg--gray--pattern--brain -> brain-pattern-white.svg (L50); bg--gray--pattern--community -> community-pattern--gray.png (L55); bg--gray--pattern--particle -> particle-pattern--white.png (L60); bg--white--pattern--brain -> brain-pattern.svg (L70); bg--white--pattern--community -> community-pattern--gray.png (L75, same file as gray's); bg--white--pattern--particle -> particle-pattern--gold.png (L80). Asset paths are not part of the token system; Figma swatches must be drawn from this exact map (see knownIssues).
geometryNotTokenized.pattern-background-size: Fixed, not a scale: [class*="--pattern--particle"] = 1400px (_background.scss:16-19); [class*="--pattern--community"] = 1000px (_background.scss:21-24); brain gets no override so it renders at the default background-size: auto auto set for any bg+pattern combo (_background.scss:11-14).
geometryNotTokenized.pattern-background-position: center center, set for any [class*="bg--"][class*="--pattern--"] combination alongside the default auto auto sizing (_background.scss:11-14).
geometryNotTokenized.pattern-opacity: MEASURED 2026-08-22 — this is the only place these levels are written down, in any of the five views. There is NO CSS opacity anywhere in the pattern system: _background-mixins.scss:120-140 emits only background-color + background-image, _background.scss:11-24 only size and position, and a live DOM check of all 12 swatches on :6007 reads opacity:1, filter:none, mix-blend-mode:normal, background-blend-mode:normal and content:none on both pseudo-elements. The strength of a pattern is ENTIRELY baked into its asset, two different ways. The four brain SVGs declare it as readable text at line 7 of each file: brain-pattern-black.svg .st0{opacity:0.15}, brain-pattern-reversed.svg 0.2, brain-pattern-white.svg 0.7, brain-pattern.svg 0.15 (brain-pattern-gray.svg declares none and is unused — not in $backgrounds). Those four are LEVELS, not distributions: exactly 5 alpha bins, ~84% zero and the rest at 25/50/75/100% of peak, i.e. line-art antialiasing. The six community/particle PNGs instead carry per-pixel alpha with 19-128 distinct values and 61-77% zero, so any single number for them is a PEAK and must be labelled one: black/community 0.212, black/particle 0.157, gold/community 0.400, gold/particle 0.271, gray/community 0.078 (black ink), gray/particle 0.898, white/community 0.078 (black ink), white/particle 0.271 (gold ink). Alpha alone never answers `how strong does this look` — gray/particle is 0.898 and yet composites to rgb(254,254,254), because it is white ink on #f3f3f3. Method, so it can be re-run: draw the asset to a canvas at natural size, read alpha via getImageData, then re-composite against the swatch's computed background-color; the analytic bg x (1-a) + ink x a matched the browser's own source-over to ±0 on all 36 channels.

behavior: Each bg--{color}[--pattern--{type}] class sets background-color via color/bg/{color} — black and gold RIDE THE BRAND CHANNELS (4.x wrote variables.$secondary/$primary = var(--brand-secondary/-primary), so grayscale retheming must keep reaching section fills; a flat gold/black alias here would re-ship the Buttons bug), gray and white are flat — plus the type-mapped foreground cascade — type 'light' (gold/gray/white) applies color/on-light/text + color/on-light/link, type 'dark' (black) applies color/on-dark/text + color/on-dark/link — through bg-fg-colors(), which every call routes through placeholders.uids-dynamic-extend($bg-class) (_background-mixins.scss:96-100, 120-140; call site _background.scss:27). That mixin keys a Sass placeholder by the literal $bg-class string and only emits the declaration body the first time a given id is seen; a later call for the SAME id is a pure @extend, not a re-declaration. add-backgrounds() is called exactly once today, so this currently behaves as a 1:1 pass-through per class — but $before/$after params exist so another selector context can request the same color's cascade again without duplicating it. An SCSS swap that inlines the color/a{color} rules directly per class instead of routing through bg-fg-colors() would silently drop that dedup path.

[class*="bg--"] forces border-color: inherit onto all descendants and their ::before/::after (_background.scss:29-40), so nested elements never carry their own border color. The actual value is set on the wrapper itself by a second, separate rule set: gray/white/gold backgrounds plus the legacy .bg-pattern--brain / .bg-pattern--brain-reversed context classes resolve to color/border/default (_background.scss:43-49); black backgrounds plus .bg--black--pattern--brain / .bg-pattern--brain-black resolve to color/border/on-dark (_background.scss:51-55).

Nested-bg link-color exceptions: under a white or gray background, prose links (p, ul, ol, dl, cite, tbody, figcaption a, excluding .bttn) are restored to var(--link-color) even though the ancestor's inherited foreground color would otherwise apply (_background.scss:57-63). But gold or black backgrounds nested one level inside white/gray revert to inherit instead, i.e. they take the ancestor's on-light foreground rather than the restored link color (_background.scss:65-71).

Pattern backgrounds set a fixed, non-tokenized background-size: particle 1400px, community 1000px; brain takes no size override and renders at the default auto auto (_background.scss:11-24; see geometryNotTokenized).
changes: 2026-08-22 — FIGMA'S PATTERN LEVELS ARE A DELIBERATE DESIGN CHANGE, NOT A FIDELITY BUG. The design system owner's ruling, taken after the measurement below rather than before it: keep the levels in component set 170:55 (black 0.30 across all three patterns; gold 0.50; gray brain 1.00, gray community 0.15, gray particle 1.00; white brain 0.15, community 0.30, particle 0.50) even though they do not match production. Do NOT 'fix' them back. Rendered against production, mean pattern ink comes out at black/brain 1.80x, black/community 1.30x, black/particle 1.56x, gold/brain 2.14x, gold/community 1.16x, gold/particle 1.54x, gray/brain 0.70x, gray/community 1.34x, gray/particle 0.85x, white/brain 1.08x, white/community 1.69x, white/particle 1.78x — scattered in BOTH directions with no common factor, so this cannot be expressed as one multiplier and there is no arithmetic that turns it back into fidelity. The design reason it is defensible: these swatches are read at thumbnail size in a documentation set, where production's true levels (a 0.149 peak on black/brain, and means around 0.017-0.14) are close to invisible. The mechanism to understand before touching it: pattern strength is baked into the asset, so a Figma paint opacity MULTIPLIES that baked alpha rather than replacing it — 170:58 renders a 0.239 peak from a 0.30 paint over an image carrying roughly 0.80 baked alpha, against production's 0.149.

2026-08-22 — WHAT THE RULING ABOVE DOES *NOT* COVER, left open deliberately. Two further defects were found by the same measurement and are NOT blessed by it. (1) IMAGE IDENTITY: Figma backs 12 combinations with only 7 distinct images. Hash 781dad9db9 serves black, gold AND gray brain, which in production are three different files with three different inks and three different opacities — and the three doc frames label that one image as brain-pattern-black.svg, brain-pattern-reversed.svg and brain-pattern-white.svg respectively, so at most one label is true. 5af416b8a9 likewise serves three particles, ab3577e809 two communities. The sharing is inverted exactly where production genuinely shares a file: gray/community and white/community both use community-pattern--gray.png, but Figma gives them two different hashes at two different opacities. Aspect ratios do not match the sources either (brain 3168x2448 = 1.29 against the 600x1201 SVG = 0.50). Wrong pictures are not a design choice, and no ruling has been taken on them. (2) THE TWO FIGMA SURFACES DISAGREE WITH EACH OTHER: all 12 doc frames (163:8 … 163:61) carry image-paint opacity 1.00 while the set carries the levels above, so a designer reading this file gets two different answers to the same question — and at 1.00 over a ~0.80-alpha image, doc frame 163:8 renders black/brain at roughly 5.3x production. Whichever way (1) is settled, these two surfaces should be made to agree. Full evidence, method and error bars are in the research fork this work came from (.claude/plans/2026-08-22_backgrounds-measurement.md there); the numbers quoted above are the conclusion.

2026-08-24 — CONSOLIDATED ONTO ONE GOVERNED SURFACE. This SUPERSEDES changes[0] and closes both defects changes[1] left open; read this entry before either of them. The design system owner's rulings; the consolidation plan they were made against lives in the research fork (.claude/plans/2026-08-24_backgrounds-consolidation-plan.md there). (a) THE FIGMA OPACITY LEVELS ARE GONE. changes[0] blessed black 0.30 / gold 0.50 / gray 1.00-0.15-1.00 / white 0.15-0.30-0.50 as a deliberate legibility change; every one is now paint opacity 1.00, because strength belongs in the asset exactly as production does it and a dial in Figma teaches Make a mechanism the system does not have. Do NOT restore the levels. (b) IMAGE IDENTITY FIXED. The 12 combos were backed by 7 images with the sharing in the wrong places; they are now backed by 11 distinct images, the single shared pair being gray/community + white/community, which is the one pair production genuinely shares (community-pattern--gray.png). Every image was uploaded from the file named in geometryNotTokenized.pattern-image-assets, and the 12 resulting Figma hashes were read back and asserted against the upload responses. (c) BRAIN IS A DOCUMENTED APPROXIMATION. The four brain SVGs cannot be tiled fills in Figma (an SVG imports as an editable vector tree, and scaleMode does not apply), so each was rasterized to PNG at 2× natural size with its authored .st0 opacity BAKED INTO THE ALPHA — 0.15/0.2/0.7/0.15 — and tiled at scalingFactor 0.5 to land back at the natural 600px that background-size: auto auto gives it. Rendering brain at full strength was considered and REJECTED: brain-pattern-black.svg, -reversed.svg and -white.svg are the same 37-path drawing with the same #FFFFFF ink and differ ONLY in that declared opacity, so full strength would have made three of the four images identical and reproduced defect (b). The rasterized peaks measured 0.149/0.200/0.698/0.149, matching the SVGs' declarations and this contract's independently-measured 0.149 for black/brain. (d) community and particle went up as the shipped PNGs unmodified, tiled at their production background-size (1000px / 1400px) rather than normalised — normalising per-pixel alpha would have produced a derived image corresponding to no file in the repo. (e) All 11 tokensUsed entries are now BOUND on the set: solid fill, text, link and border. The border tokens had been bound nowhere in Figma; they are now on a bordered sample rectangle inside each variant, which documents behavior[1] (descendants inherit border-color; the wrapper sets the value) rather than decorating the swatch edge. The doc frames' own strokes had been an unbound #000000 at opacity 0.133 — a hand-typed near-miss of color/border/default's 0.125, and wrong-signed on black. (f) NOT YET DONE — the 16 doc frames (163:5 … 163:61) are superseded but STILL IN THE FILE. Deleting them was blocked in-session: the Figma MCP's safety classifier refuses a use_figma script that removes pre-existing content, while allowing reads, property mutations, and removal of nodes the script itself created (both probed 2026-08-24). Until a human deletes them this page still has two surfaces that disagree, and the frames are the stale one — they carry the 7-image sharing, the unbound 0.133 strokes and the old labels. Do not resolve the disagreement by editing the frames.
knownIssues: Legacy classes .bg-pattern--brain, .bg-pattern--brain-reversed and .bg-pattern--brain-black are referenced in 6 UIDS files (mostly as ancestor context: _background.scss:47,52; _headline-mixins.scss:103; blockquote.scss; tables.scss; base/_paragraph.scss:174 — stat.scss:182's '&.bg-pattern--brain-reversed' is a SELF-compound on the stat element, the one exception) plus 7 more in uiowa/uiowa's uids_base (global.scss, layout-builder.scss, cta.scss, forms.scss, main-menu.scss, headings.scss, admin/_claro.scss) — but DEFINED nowhere: no producer exists in uiowa/uiowa code or config. Every layout_builder_styles.style.*.yml classes: value ships only the current grammar (bg--{color}--pattern--{type}), verified across all 31 background style configs (16 component + 15 section), never these bare legacy names. They survive only via editor-entered classes in old DB content. Keep as context selectors; never tokenize as color/pattern option values — no code path produces them.

DOWNSTREAM: uids_base's two adjacent-section padding-merge lists DISAGREE. global.scss:189-196 uses EXACT selectors (.bg--gold/.bg--black/.bg--gray — no bg--white — plus the three legacy brain names), so current-style combined pattern classes (bg--gold--pattern--particle etc.) never merge there: an exact .bg--gold cannot match the single class token bg--gold--pattern--particle. layout-builder.scss:220-228 instead uses SUBSTRING matchers ([class*="bg--gold"] etc., plus bg--white and the same legacy names), which DO match the combined pattern classes — so merge behavior differs between the two contexts, and the front-end (global.scss) is the one that misses pattern backgrounds. Fix belongs in uiowa/uiowa, not here.

[class*="bg--"] / [class*="bg--gold"] / [class*="--pattern--particle"] substring matching (rather than exact class matching) IS this system's public API — border-color inheritance, link-color overrides, and downstream padding-merge all key off it with no explicit contract otherwise. This is documented and FROZEN, not a bug: renaming any grammar segment (bg--, a color name, or --pattern--) breaks these selectors across 8+ files in two repos — the class grammar (see options) is the thing to treat as the versioned public shape.

The 16 bg--{color}[--pattern--{type}] combos (background.ts allBackgroundOptions) do not each have a unique image: bg--gray--pattern--community and bg--white--pattern--community both use community-pattern--gray.png; bg--white--pattern--brain uses brain-pattern.svg while bg--gray--pattern--brain uses the distinct brain-pattern-white.svg. Full per-combo map (from _background-mixins.scss's $backgrounds, $imgpath = '../../assets/images'): black -> brain-pattern-black.svg / community-pattern--black.png / particle-pattern--black.png; gold -> brain-pattern-reversed.svg / community-pattern--white.png / particle-pattern.png; gray -> brain-pattern-white.svg / community-pattern--gray.png / particle-pattern--white.png; white -> brain-pattern.svg / community-pattern--gray.png (shared with gray) / particle-pattern--gold.png. Figma swatches must be drawn from this exact map, not assumed to be 12 distinct images.
